headline: South Asia: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all territory seized by Houthis
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all territory seized by Houthis.
- Western Russia: Three killed and six injured in Russian attacks on Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts.
- Asia: Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as Germany’s Merz visits, pledges aid.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: UDC warns it cannot guarantee daily services at Little Dunn’s River.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: UDC warns it cannot guarantee daily services at Little Dunn’s River.
The Urban Development Corporation (UDC) says the relevant team has been directed to take steps to facilitate public access to Little Dunn’s River Beach in Ocho Rios, St Ann, in compliance with a court order. However, the UDC indicated that it was not in a position at this time to provide “day-to-day management” of the popular recreational spot, including arrangements for security, lifeguard services, sanitation, maintenance or other amenities ordinarily required for such a facility. The UDC is the state entity that owns the facility.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Docs to decide on next steps in response to delayed IDT ruling.
More than 100 junior doctors at the Mandeville Regional Hospital in Manchester stayed off the job on Friday, joining hundreds of colleagues across the island. The junior doctors abstained from work in an effort to pressure the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to give a ruling in its overtime and incentive dispute with the Government or outline a timeline for its award.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Three killed and six injured in Russian attacks on Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Three killed and six injured in Russian attacks on Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts.
Russian FPV drone and artillery strikes killed three people and injured six across Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts on 4 October.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Zelenskyy surprised by Russia's "savage desire" to escalate war, says it was Russia that struck first.
Speaking alongside Friedrich Merz, President Zelenskyy rejected Russian pretexts for escalation after strikes hit Kyiv's bridges and data networks.
- The Moscow Times, 11 hours ago: Russia to Intensify Strikes on Ukraine After Zelensky Interview.
Moscow said Russian forces would step up attacks on military facilities, defense industry sites and related infrastructure.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Reaching the core: could Russia cut Ukrainians off from the internet and mobile communications?.
Over the past week, the Kremlin has been expanding its campaign of terror to include new targets. In addition to hitting energy infrastructure and logistics hubs, Russia is now attacking the data centres that house equipment used by internet service providers, government services, banks and other digital systems, launching a wave of strikes on buildings where vital telecoms infrastructure is concentrated.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Moscow says it will step up strikes on Ukraine after Kyiv vows to hit Russian oil refineries.
- Politico Europe, 10 hours ago: Moscow says it will step up strikes on Ukraine after Kyiv vows to hit Russian oil refineries.
Russia's announcement came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country would “have to respond in any way we can” to Russian attacks.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: $38M from federal government to KPMG during ban.
Happy Labour Day and welcome to the newsletter that makes you think harder. If you’ve been forwarded this Playbook, you can sign up free to get it each weekday morning. ESSENTIALS — KPMG raking it in, despite ban on new work — Surprise compliments for Chris Bowen — One Nation and Liberal paths to power […]

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: 'Drone Strike On El Obeid Shelter Kills Boy, Wounds 12 Children'.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Sudan: 'Drone Strike On El Obeid Shelter Kills Boy, Wounds 12 Children'.
[Dabanga] El Obeid -- A drone strike on a shelter for internally displaced people in El Obeid, North Kordofan, late on Thursday reportedly killed a boy and wounded 12 children, as another drone strike on a university dormitory in the city killed five civilians and injured 47 others.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 6 hours ago: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Captures Tigray Capital As Its Regional Rivals Meet in Egypt.
[RFI] Ethiopian federal forces have regained control of the Tigray rebels' regional capital, local sources said on Sunday, while Ethiopia's regional rivals gathered in Egypt to discuss the risk of a wider war.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 6 hours ago: Ethiopia: Tigray Rebels Reportedly Abandon Capital As Ethiopian Government Forces Advance.
[RFI] Tigray rebels are abandoning their regional capital in northern Ethiopia, local residents said on Saturday, as pro-government forces advanced on the city. The region is in the grip of the worst fighting since the civil war of 2020-2022.
- Africanews, 17 hours ago: At least 17 people killed in Kenya road crash, most of them Catholic pilgrims.
A crash involving multiple vehicles on a highway to the Kenyan coastal city of Mombasa on Saturday killed 17 people, most of them pilgrims on the way to a prayer site, officials said.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: The flydubai attack was a failure before it was a plot - analysis.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: The flydubai attack was a failure before it was a plot - analysis.
Officials in Oman and Australia reportedly raised concerns about the flydubai co-pilot. Whatever the Iran probe finds, investigators must explain why the warnings failed to stop him from flying.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: War on Iran: Is escalation more likely than a deal?.
Former Iranian and US diplomats agree that the war on Iran is likely to get worse in the coming weeks.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, 6 hours ago: Germany’s Merz in Kyiv announces $1.5B in aid, urges Putin to end war.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, on a surprise visit to Kyiv, announced $1.5 billion in military and reconstruction aid
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Nearly three years after Oct. 7, Israeli donations keep climbing as philanthropy shifts to recovery.
JGive CEO Ori Ben-Shlomo says donations rose from NIS 160 million before Oct. 7 to nearly NIS 400 million last year, as Israeli philanthropy shifts from emergency relief toward rehabilitation.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all territory seized by Houthis.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all territory seized by Houthis.
Yemen’s leader announced on Sunday the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the group made fresh gains on the ground, effectively encircling a government-held city. The announcement sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost swathes of the country’s Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait — a chokepoint for international shipping — after a lightning offensive by Houthis.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 19 hours ago: Yemen offensive.
IT appears that escalation is on the cards where the Houthi-Saudi and US-Iran conflicts are concerned. As per reports, Riyadh is planning an offensive to help the Yemeni government — which it backs — retake the strategically important Red Sea coast area from the pro-Iran Houthis, who captured it during a lightning offensive last month. Hostilities are continuing; there were reports on Saturday of both Riyadh and Sana’a being attacked. Meanwhile, members of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement are due to hold an emergency meeting to discuss the Yemen situation.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: PTI terms access to Imran 'principal point of deadlock', claims Centre refused to include it in agreement.
The PTI on Sunday asserted that the main reason for the breakdown of its talks with the Centre was that the latter refused to incorporate terms regarding access to incarcerated party founder Imran Khan into a proposed agreement. Hours-long negotiations yesterday between an opposition delegation comprising the PTI and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), and a joint team of the government and PPP, ended in a deadlock.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: 'We are not yes-men': CM Afridi launches PTI long march to Islamabad, convoy enters Karak district.
PESHAWAR/LAKKI MARWAT/DI KHAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday launched the PTI’s long march towards Islamabad from Lakki Marwat, saying the party would “not accept” any policy that was against the interests of the people of KP. The PTI has gone ahead with its march despite warnings from the federal government, which has vowed to prevent any violent gatherings in the capital. The protest aims to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan.
Asia - bottom line: Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as Germany’s Merz visits, pledges aid.
- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, Politico Europe, 4 hours ago: Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as Germany’s Merz visits, pledges aid.
Russia struck a bridge in Kyiv on Sunday soon after Germany’s chancellor arrived in Ukraine’s capital on a surprise visit to demonstrate European support in the face of an upsurge in attacks. Air raid sirens blared across Kyiv, urging residents to shelter soon after Friedrich Merz arrived under tight security, with warnings of approaching Russian attack drones. - South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: Ukraine believes Russia shared jet-drone technology with North Korea, says Zelensky.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sunday ⁠he believed Russia ⁠may have shared jet-drone technology ⁠with its long-standing ally North Korea. In recent weeks, Russia has sharply increased its use of jet-drones against Ukraine, which so far has no effective means of countering them other than using ‌combat aircraft. Earlier in the war, North Korea supplied Russia with millions of artillery shells and it has since provided ballistic missiles that Moscow regularly uses to attack...
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Iran tells US there is no military solution to Middle East war.
Iran’s top diplomat insisted on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States’ war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending the conflict apparently at an impasse. A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure. India - bottom line: Watch: Massive fire at Saudi Aramco sites targeted in Houthi missile, drone strikes.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: Watch: Massive fire at Saudi Aramco sites targeted in Houthi missile, drone strikes.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: 1 dead as Russian drones hit desi pharma plant in Ukraine.
In Ukraine's Sumy region, six Russian drones attacked the Kusum Group's pharmaceutical plant, killing one engineer and injuring others. The main structure of the facility was largely destroyed during the targeted strike, which occurs amid a pattern of similar attacks. The company estimates damage from this incident could exceed $50 million, impacting operations significantly.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 12 hours ago: Did Israel ignore warnings? UAE shared info about flydubai crew & Omani co-pilot.
The UAE shared passenger and crew information with Israel before a FlyDubai flight whose Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain and tried to seize control, AP reported. The co-pilot had reportedly been barred from flying by Oman over extremist concerns before joining FlyDubai. The incident has raised questions over Israel’s foreign-flight security system, despite previous warnings about inadequate checks and limited resources within the Transportation Ministry.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan.
Justice Ujjal Bhuyan condemned the extensive deletion of voter names from electoral rolls due to the special intensive revision process. He emphasized that such actions undermine the core principles of the Indian Constitution and disenfranchise millions of citizens. Bhuyan highlighted that the right to vote is essential for free and fair elections in India. He urged that no citizen should be denied the right to vote without due process.

North Korea launched a missile toward waters off its eastern coast on Saturday, with the weapon striking a designated target about 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) away in the East Sea (Sea of Japan), according to the country’s state media Sunday. Australia - bottom line: 19yo driver allegedly rammed rideshare with two people inside.
- ABC News Australia, just now: 19yo driver allegedly rammed rideshare with two people inside.
A 19-year-old driver who allegedly rammed a rideshare vehicle carrying two passengers has been arrested in Adelaide's north, with SA Police also responding to several other crashes, including one in which a 53-year-old man was killed.

Marnus Labuschagne makes his case to keep the number three spot in Friday's first Test against South Africa, with a timely century in a warm-up match.
- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: Two pedestrians killed after being hit by car.
Two men aged 70 and 55 have died after being hit by an SUV at Tura Beach, north of Merimbula, with the driver taken to hospital for mandatory testing.

Rain and possible isolated severe storms are forecast for south-east Queensland as school resumes on Tuesday, while the northern coast stays mostly fine and the west remains hot.
